data.name: Label18.ToolTip
data.value: Attributed stall speed of converter. The true stall speed attained with WOT applied while the tranny output speed remains zero. Used to estimate converter slip when unlocked and used in the stall logic calculations.

data.name: Label24.ToolTip
data.value: Gear that converter lockup occurs under normal acceleration. Assuming all three relavent rules that govern are still enabled, typical appication on a 6 speed transmission with a value of 3 would be 1>2, 2>3, Lockup, 3>4, 4>5, 5>6. With ever following gear being came into already locked. Not recommened on 4Lxx transmissions. Even with the "shift lock" enabled, there are to many things that can cause a converter unlock during a shift on gen III pcms. Since we do not have access to all those parameters and the original calibrations are just not setup for it, poor results usually result and you get shift, unlock, relock situations. Accel lock being 4th gear is recommended for all 4 speeds.

data.name: StallLogic.ToolTipText
data.value: Stall logic tries to estimate the difference in rpm beteen locked and unlocked converter states. The idea is to prevent harsh lockups that result from a large difference between locked and unlocked. Stall Logic causes the driver to either decrease throttle before locking or speeding up to a speed that the converter is not a loose acting.

data.name: Label21.ToolTip
data.value: Max downshift rpm. Limits the rpm the engine can come into during a downshift. Normally left maxed out for cars. Used for tow haul modes in trucks to prevent run away downshifts when pulling a trailer or heavy load (ie 3500). Can also be used in cars to increase the spread between wot up and down shifts when spinning is a problem or even to keep a lazy transmission out of the limiter after a max effort downshift that was to close to the next upshift.
